title: North star for exits: real-time P(SL before TP | trade state now) and an exit-now mechanism that turns would-be losers into winners
note: [2026-10-14T21:05Z manager session_01VduHYzdaXe27wTDBLSu8ao] OPERATOR 2026-10-14 ~21:04Z, verbatim: 'So definitely, like, knowing when a trade is going to be giving back a lot and a trade is valuable. But really where we want to get to is knowing, like, being able to assess the trade in real time well enough to know when we should, like, drop out early, right? So even if the TP is, like, close, if the momentum suddenly turns, then, like, what are the chances of, you know, that, like, at any given moment, are we going to hit the stop loss before we hit the take profit? That's basically the question, right? And if it's the stop loss, then we need a mechanism for knowing, like, when the right time to drop out of trading in real time is, basically. Like, that's where we want to head. Not just avoiding trades where there's give back, but improving them so that they turn from bad trades to good trades. Because many of them are good trades. They just, we get sometimes even very close to the TP, and sometimes not close, but it still could have been a good trade if we just knew to get out in time.' MANAGER READING: the target is a first-passage model evaluated at every bar of an open trade (P(SL hit before TP | state at bar t)) plus an exit policy (exit now when the expected value of holding falls below exiting, net of cost), graded by net P&L per capital-day vs the fixed bracket. Today this exists only piecemeal: P1-Q5 momentum-turn label study (blocked/RQ-20261014-9807-05, blocked on per-bar path data), P2-Q3 rung 3.3 per-bar in-trade history (scheduled W3).
